verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Brent Approaches $97 Trigger; Iran Suspends Talks; 30Y Day-2 Fails
verdict.rationale_short: Iran suspended peace talks and threatened full Hormuz closure, sending Brent to $94.98 — just $2.02 from the XLE short's mandatory cover trigger. The 30Y re-broke 5.00% intraday on the Iran headline (spiked to 4.518% on the 10Y), failing the Day-2 sub-5.0% confirmation needed for the NVDA add. NVDA itself reversed the morning's chip-curb selloff and closed ~$221 on RTX Spark product depth at COMPUTEX — a positive surprise — but the 30Y condition remains unmet. GOOGL fell to $380.34, below the $384 entry zone floor and approaching the $378 invalidation. Step aside: trim XLE short to ≤25% now; hold NVDA with stop raised to $215; initiate no new longs until Iran clarity and 30Y Day-2 confirmation both arrive.

bear_case: The June 1 session inverted the central macro narrative of the prior nine weeks: Iran has suspended talks, threatened full Hormuz closure, and oil has risen 5-6% in a single session. Brent at $94.98 is a single bad overnight headline from forcing an involuntary cover of the XLE short at a loss. The 30Y's second consecutive failure to close below 5.00% means the rate-confirmation sequence that was supposed to unlock the NVDA add and the high-conviction BUY upgrade has been reset by Iran risk. GOOGL's decline to $380.34 — the morning's 'cleanest fresh long' — illustrates that broad-market breadth is narrower than the index prints suggest: only NVDA/MSFT and energy were green. If Iran rhetoric hardens overnight and Brent opens above $97, the XLE short converts to a loss and the 30Y re-targets 5.05-5.10%, requiring an immediate Step Aside across all positions. Invalidation: Brent closes above $97 with 30Y above 5.05% — the framework converts to bearish; exit all longs simultaneously.
